item.title: Canonical residual physics-informed neural networks and algorithmic perturbation landscapes map cell-fate transitions in longitudinal H3K27M glioma
item.description: arXiv:2610.33000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pediatric high-grade glioma is a dynamically heterogeneous disease in which therapeutic selection pressures, microenvironmental selection and developmental plasticity can reorganize cellular-state structure over time. Here we investigated these adaptive behaviors in glioma dynamics from single-cell ecologies by merging physics-driven artificial intelligence and complex systems theory. Specifically, this study explores canonical residual-based physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), dynamical systems modelling comparators, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and Block Decomposition Method (BDM) perturbation analysis to understand glioma cell fate decisions. The primary analyses distinguished longitudinal initial from recurrent H3K27M cells and, within the recurrent specimen set, stem/progenitor-like from differentiated/glial-like annotation-derived states. Across five-fold cross-validation, RD achieved AUC $0.995 \pm 0.005$ and macro-F1 $0.973 \pm 0.016$ for initial--recurrence discrimination, and AUC $0.698 \pm 0.012$ and macro-F1 $0.629 \pm 0.014$ for recurrent-state subtype discrimination. FP achieved AUC $0.931 \pm 0.018$ and $0.665 \pm 0.012$, respectively. Cross-model XAI repeatedly prioritized PTGDS, CHI3L1, IGFBP7, SPARCL1 and NRXN3 in longitudinal progression. BDM perturbation rankings emphasized heat-shock/stress-response and immune-associated network signatures. These findings are candidate computational network biomarkers rather than experimentally established causal signatures. The study provides a reproducible bridge between physics-constrained latent dynamics, interpretable gene attribution, and data-driven algorithmic perturbation landscapes for in silico pattern generation about glioma cell fate plasticity and early recurrence detection.
item.dc:creator: Abicumaran Uthamacumaran

item.title: A unified and composable framework for modeling packed-bed liquid chromatography
item.description: arXiv:2610.33269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Packed-bed chromatography is a cornerstone of bioseparation, yet its modeling landscape remains fragmented by numerous model variants, inconsistent terminology, and limited structural clarity. While prior work has categorized and contrasted individual variants, our approach shifts the focus to unification. We present a unified, modular, and composable framework that integrates diverse mechanistic packed-bed chromatography models into a coherent structure. Starting from a high-resolution three-dimensional model, the framework systematically derives a hierarchy of reduced-order models through formal model order reduction. It encompasses a broad range of bulk transport phenomena, intraparticle mass transfer processes, binding mechanisms, and chemical reactions. Formulated orthogonally, these modules are independently meaningful and can be systematically combined into mathematically consistent models tailored to specific applications. The framework recovers and generalizes existing models, establishes a consistent taxonomy, and enables novel model combinations and extensions, including alternative column and particle geometries, particle-size and particle-type distributions, component-specific pore accessibility, rapid-equilibrium binding and reaction formulations, and size-exclusion with simultaneous binding. The framework is accessible through CADET-Equations, an interactive web application for model assembly and automatic generation of governing equations in LaTeX, promoting standardization and transparency. Its design principles are increasingly reflected throughout the CADET ecosystem, whose modular architecture supports the majority of the proposed model family. The generality and composable design of the framework provide a foundation for extending chromatography modeling software toward integrated bioseparation processes and advanced computational biotechnology applications.
item.dc:creator: Jan Michael Breuer, Samuel Leweke, Johannes Schm\"older, Antonia Berger, Gregor J. Gassner, Eric von Lieres
